controls.trigger: terminal closure, shell change, conversation change, restart, or operator handoff
controls.required_behavior: Persist repo/head, network classification, target lock, lane, package set, expected state, latest run, cleanup state, completed work, evidence path, and exact next action outside the repository working tree.
controls.forbidden_behavior: Require the operator to re-explain terminal, network, target, lane, or prior failure state.

controls.trigger: command requires public Internet/GitHub access or protected target/share access
controls.required_behavior: Classify the current network and print the required network before execution; wrong-network failures stop early with one exact next action.
controls.forbidden_behavior: Run unrelated diagnostics or protected target operations on the Internet/Guest lane, or Git refresh operations on the protected-only lane by assumption.

controls.required_behavior: Use repository-owned launchers that do not depend on pre-existing interactive variables or shell fragments and behave consistently from CMD and PowerShell.
controls.forbidden_behavior: Require operators to reconstruct multi-page PowerShell, paste try/catch/finally blocks, or switch shells to continue the same lane.

controls.trigger: deployment consumes multiple packages or a bundle from an approved source
controls.required_behavior: Validate every required package source, entrypoint, actual file inventory, hashes, and catalog drift before target contact or mutation where practical and always before staging or execution.
controls.forbidden_behavior: Start target staging while any required source remains unresolved or invent a replacement filename for stale bundle metadata.

controls.trigger: workflow creates remote staging, scheduled tasks, generated evidence, or other transient resources
controls.required_behavior: One tracked process owns stage, execute, retrieve, profile, cleanup, and final evidence for a unique run ID.
controls.forbidden_behavior: Move cleanup into an interactive follow-up fragment or broad-delete shared directories.

controls.trigger: latest run failed, terminal crashed, cleanup is missing, or cleanup is unproven
controls.required_behavior: Inspect exact run evidence, recover any run-owned checkpoint/result, clean only exact run-owned resources, verify absence, and preserve proven completed work before a new mutation begins.
controls.forbidden_behavior: Blindly start a new deployment or repeat work already proven complete.

controls.trigger: multi-phase command, dispatcher, wrapper, or long-running field operation
controls.required_behavior: Write stable phase/package checkpoints as proof boundaries and propagate every nonzero child exit code to the caller and final artifact.
controls.forbidden_behavior: Return success while a child command, evidence dispatcher, cleanup step, or required phase failed.

controls.trigger: tracked package metadata differs from the actual approved source tree
controls.required_behavior: Record expected versus actual inventory, missing/unexpected files, hashes, and drift interpretation; choose one explicit bundle authority and fail or proceed according to that tracked policy.
controls.forbidden_behavior: Silently ignore drift, guess a missing file, or partially stage a bundle before the drift decision is recorded.

controls.trigger: a changed surface fails or new code needs merge proof
controls.required_behavior: Run parse/schema/static/contract checks for changed surfaces first, classify failures as changed-surface or baseline, rerun the failed gate after repair, and broaden only when the declared proof ceiling requires it.
controls.forbidden_behavior: Expand into unrelated architecture or diagnostics while the owning changed-surface failure remains unresolved.

known_failure_patterns.signal: operator command points at missing or outdated machine-local launcher content
portable launcher mishandles a normal Windows drive path
evidence recovery crashes when zero matching artifacts exist
wrapper returns exit zero after an inner evidence or deployment failure
Windows-native operator flow unexpectedly requires Git Bash, python3, or an interactive shell-specific variable
tracked source inventory references a file that no longer exists in the approved package bundle
target staging or task creation starts before all required package sources are proven ready
operator is instructed to paste a standalone finally/cleanup fragment after the owning process has ended
operator must restate terminal, network, target, lane, expected state, or latest run before work can resume
field window is consumed by broad unrelated tests instead of the smallest changed-surface validator and next actionable gate
